reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen because autonomous reasoning can quickly identify shared structural patterns across instances, while external XAI tools provide quantitative, model-agnostic attribution scores to validate spurious feature influence. This combination increases the robustness of detecting features that are common, high-attribution, and semantically unrelated to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 44852) and list their values across each instance.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features with their observed values in each instance

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status, relationship) is semantically related to income class, or if it appears to be a spurious correlation due to co-occurrence with known predictors.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A brief explanation of whether any shared feature is semantically meaningful or spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable feature importance across instances, enabling detection of high-attribution features shared among misclassifications. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations to validate how spurious features influence predictions. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature significantly alters predictions, indicating its causal (or spurious) role. Together, they strengthen the identification of truly spurious, shared features.
